rationale: Objective is the per-rank summed NCCL device-kernel duration, max across ranks, median over 3 separately profiled steps: baseline samples [54.868, 40.490, 53.625] ms (rank 1 [54.87, 40.49, 53.63] vs rank 0 [35.73, 36.03, 36.00]). All communication in the step is 13 f32 SUM allreduces on the default NCCL group (12x 28,351,488 B buckets + 1x 157,541,376 B bucket = 497,759,232 B), dispatched by the DDP reducer during the last microbatch's backward; both allreduce call records (d0938de87369efd500322679, 12 invocations; b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b, 1 invocation) are children of the project invoke call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0. Measured both-peers-ready references (collective_calibration, separate warmed worker): ~1.99-2.01 ms per 28.35 MB and ~10.58-10.63 ms per 157.5 MB collective, i.e. a wire floor of about 34.6 ms for the step's bytes; bytes themselves are not reducible because gradients must stay fp32, bit-identical across ranks and reference-matched. Rank 0's clean kernel sum (~36.0 ms) already sits ~1.4 ms above that floor, while the max rank carries 6-19 ms of in-kernel spin waiting (rank 1 in the clean baseline; rank 0 in the independent execution_timeline capture, 45.6 vs 35.6 ms; rank 0's 196.1 ms in the perturbed discovery capture is not used quantitatively). The waiting mass is created by the baseline schedule: no_sync on 3 of 4 microbatches and 13 per-bucket collectives interleaved into a CPU-launch-bound eager backward produce 13 rank-arrival sync points (compute overlap measured at only 7.7-11.3 ms of the 45.6 ms comm union). The coherent editable boundary is therefore the complete accumulated-step region (project invoke) plus the two nested allreduce groups it owns: rewrite the step so gradient synchronization executes once, after all backward compute, as a single fused allreduce over a flat fp32 copy of the locally accumulated gradients (pre-divide by world_size, SUM on the default NCCL group, in-place copy back into .grad before optimizer.step), with the DDP reducer left idle via no_sync on all 4 microbatches. Per-element arithmetic stays identical to the DDP default hook (divide by world_size then SUM), preserving exact cross-rank gradient equality (atol=0, rtol=0), the serial global-batch reference and post-step parameter checks; zero_grad stays inside the timed region and the only collectives in the clean timing path remain the step's own real NCCL gradient synchronization.
hypothesis: Replacing 13 interleaved bucket allreduces with one post-backward fused 497,759,232 B collective removes ~12 rank-arrival sync events (measured max-rank excess over the both-peers-ready floor implies ~0.9-1.5 ms of accumulated spin per sync point) and 12 per-collective ramp/drain/launch overheads, so the diagnostic max-rank kernel-sum should fall from 53.6 ms toward the wire floor, plausibly to ~35-38 ms (~30% reduction) with lower sample variance (baseline spread 40.5-54.9 ms). Treated as unproven: a fused 497 MB collective was never observed (extrapolated from the measured ~14.2-14.8 GB/s logical payload rate at the two observed sizes); arrival skew at the single remaining sync point could still show a tail event, though bounded by one skew sample instead of 13; and the step_ms constraint has only ~5.8 ms headroom (<=1.05x the 115.1 ms median-of-max) because the rewrite forfeits the measured 7.7-11.3 ms of comm/compute overlap while removing the waiting rank's in-kernel spin - net wall-clock and objective effect must be verified by measurement, including the fp32 flat-buffer copy traffic (~1-2 ms) and unchanged correctness/negative-control outcomes.
